name: intraday-equities-multi3-h03-gru
notes: GRU over the 20-step lag path, last step to a linear head. Same three split-free tradables, same twenty folds, same ADR-0059 label (SPY-residual, divided by a causal 390-minute sigma times sqrt(h)) as run-multi3-h20-ridge.json and its LightGBM twin: the scan node's estimator block is the ONLY difference, so a gap is the architecture. Reached through ADR-0061's ZooEstimator, which splits the row by NAME - the twenty ret_lag_* columns are the time axis, the other 67 columns ride as constant channels over it. PRE-REGISTERED BAR, declared before the run: worth pursuing only if it clears BOTH >10% of the 60 name-folds at p<.05 (ridge 6.7%, LightGBM 5.0%, null 5%) AND a mean val MSPE under ridge's 1.345. hpo_trials is 0 on purpose: A0036 showed the inner holdout cannot rank models at this SNR, so the hyperparameters are fixed and declared rather than searched. HORIZON: this document asks about H=3 minute(s) ONLY - lead_start=lead_stop=3 (ADR-0062), so the training label and the single walked lead are both 1. The H=20 family trained at 5 and walked 5/10/15/20; these are a different question on the same cohort, folds and label, not a re-run. Run to resolve WHY H=1 rejected 40% of name-folds with a +0.09% MSPE gain while H=20/30/60 sat at the null with a negative one. Bid-ask bounce predicts the gain decays like 1/h (the label always contains px[t], but its variance grows with h), so ~+0.045% at H=2 and ~+0.03% at H=3. A gain that decays SLOWER than that is not bounce.

features.notes: lookback=20 emits one-minute ret_lag columns for the last 20 minutes. Every horizon here is cross_session so none costs rows beyond a one-time warmup; see docs/research/row-loss-is-intra-session-scale-warmup-not-cross-session.md.

tradable.notes: SPY has already entered the residual features; score tradables.

scan.notes: GRU over the 20-step lag path, last step to a linear head. Fixed hyperparameters, no search. Adam, MSE, 30 epochs at lr 3e-3 on standardised columns - the same training block for all three archs, so the comparison is the architecture and not its schedule. The grid is the single lead 1: h* is 1 or nothing, and the Clark-West p IS the test at that horizon.

names.notes: The three split-free tradables. Sits after tradable so the cohort that built the cross-sectional features (all five plus SPY) is untouched; only what gets SCORED narrows.

walkforward.notes: Same post-COVID folds as run-hstar-cv-postcovid.json so the two are comparable: first validation 2022-05-06, twenty 63-day steps, a real 730-day bounded training window, last validation inside the 2025-11-30 cut. objective is val_ic, NOT go_frac: counting fold-level rejections and taking the max is vote counting, which Hedges-Olkin showed is inconsistent when per-fold power is below one half (A0035). The winner here only labels a fold in the summary; the science is the per-fold sequence, which is what the block-by-block reading needs. embargo_days=5 is now larger than any label window on this grid (20 minutes), so no training row's label can reach into validation.
